ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On a horizontal surface, a wooden board is pulled by two ropes, each making an angle of $\theta=22.5^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The tension in each rope is $F=250N$. The board moves at a constant velocity for a distance of $20m$ in $15s$. Given that $\cos 22.5^{\circ} \approx 0.9$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the resistance force $f$.

2. Calculate the work done by the tension forces in the two ropes.
3. Calculate the total power of the tension forces in the two ropes.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: On a horizontal surface, a wooden board is pulled by two ropes, each making an angle of $\theta=22.5^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The tension in each rope is $F=250N$. The board moves at a constant velocity for a distance of $20m$ in $15s$. Given that $\cos 22.5^{\circ} \approx 0.9$. 1. Determine the magnitude of the resistance force $f$. 2. Calculate the work done by the tension forces in the two ropes. 3. Calculate the total power of the tension forces in the two ropes.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure is a vertically placed wooden board, and two ropes are pulled obliquely from the left side onto the wooden board; beside each rope there is a horizontal dashed line as a reference, and the angle θ with the horizontal line is marked. The displacement of the wooden board's motion is horizontal, so when the tension does work on the horizontal displacement, only the horizontal component of the tension is taken. Reasoning: The tension in each rope is F = 250 N, the angle with the horizontal is θ = 22.5°, and cos 22.5° ≈ 0.9. Therefore, the horizontal pulling-force component of one rope is F cosθ = 250 × 0.9 = 225 N. The total horizontal pulling force of the two ropes is 2F cosθ = 2 × 225 = 450 N. The wooden board moves at a constant speed, and the resultant force in the horizontal direction is zero, so the magnitude of the resistance is equal to the total horizontal pulling force, namely f = 450 N. The tension does work on the horizontal displacement, contributed only by the horizontal component. The wooden board moves a distance s = 20 m, and the total work done by the tensions of the two ropes is W = 2Fs cosθ = 2 × 250 × 20 × 0.9 = 9000 J = 9.0 × 10^3 J. The motion time t = 15 s, and the total power is P = W/t = 9000/15 = 600 W.
